## Installation

First install [`ir`](https://r-lib.github.io/ir/#installation). Then install
`rush` as an `ir` tool, which puts a `rush` launcher on your `PATH`:

```sh
ir tool install github::jeroenjanssens/rush
```

That's it; there's no separate R package to load. The first time a command
needs a package (say, ggplot2 for a plot), `ir` fetches and caches it for you.

## Quick tour

Evaluate an expression. The value of the last expression is printed:

```{term}
rush run '6 * 7'
```

Read from standard input with `-`. Input is read into a data frame called `df`,
so `seq 6` becomes a one-column table you can compute on:

```{term}
seq 6 | rush run -H '2 * sum(df$x1)' -
```

Give `rush run` a file and it is read into `df` before your expression runs.
With no expression, the data frame is simply printed back out, a handy way to
peek at a file:

```{term}
rush run -o mtcars.csv 'mtcars'
rush run 'head(df, 5)' mtcars.csv
```

Because `rush` writes plain CSV to standard output, you can keep piping into the
next command, including another `rush`:

```{term}
rush run 'head(df, 10)' mtcars.csv | rush run 'df |> dplyr::select(mpg, cyl, hp, wt)' -
```

Load extra packages with `-l`, or enter the whole Tidyverse with `-t`:

```{term}
rush run -t 'count(df, cyl, sort = TRUE)' mtcars.csv
```

Query files directly with SQL:

```{term}
rush sql "SELECT cyl, ROUND(AVG(mpg), 1) AS avg_mpg, COUNT(*) AS n
          FROM mtcars GROUP BY cyl ORDER BY avg_mpg DESC" mtcars.csv
```

Convert between formats in one step:

```{term}
rush convert -o mtcars.parquet mtcars.csv
rush run 'nrow(df)' mtcars.parquet
```

Draw a quick terminal plot:

```{term}
rush plot -x wt -y mpg -c cyl -O ansi --width 72 mtcars.csv
```

```{term}
#| include: false
rm -f mtcars.csv mtcars.parquet
```
